holidays.name: Argyle Sweater Day
holidays.description: A day to dust off your most diamond-patterned knitwear and wear an argyle sweater with pride, whether it's preppy, grandpa-chic, or golf-course ready.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance that spread through social media and novelty-holiday calendars. It celebrates the argyle pattern, which is based on the tartan of the Campbell clan of Argyll in western Scotland.
holidays.funFact: Argyle patterns became a worldwide fashion staple in the 20th century after the Duke of Windsor wore them, and golfers helped make them popular on the course.

holidays.name: Bubble Bath Day
holidays.description: An invitation to fill the tub with bubbles, light a candle, and soak away the stress of the post-holiday blues. Rubber duckies are encouraged.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial wellness-and-relaxation observance listed in many novelty holiday calendars. It appears to have been created to give people a cozy reason to unwind in the cold, gloomy days of early January.
holidays.funFact: The word 'bubble bath' wasn't common until the 20th century, when shops started selling foaming bath products, although people have added scents and oils to baths for thousands of years.

holidays.name: Elvis Presley's Birthday
holidays.description: Fans around the world celebrate the King of Rock and Roll with sequined jumpsuits, peanut butter and banana sandwiches, and lip-curling karaoke renditions of 'Hound Dog.'
holidays.origin: Elvis Aaron Presley was born on January 8, 1935, in Tupelo, Mississippi. Fans keep the date alive with tribute concerts and parties, and Graceland holds annual birthday celebrations.
holidays.funFact: Elvis had a stillborn identical twin brother named Jesse Garon Presley. Elvis was reportedly 'the one who lived.'

holidays.name: Show and Tell Day at Work
holidays.description: A day to bring something meaningful, odd, or impressive to the office and share it with your coworkers, just like in elementary school but with more PowerPoint.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance that adapts the classic grade-school activity for adults. It encourages workplace bonding and getting to know the quirky side of your colleagues.
holidays.funFact: Show and tell has been a staple of American classrooms since the early 20th century, and it is meant to help kids build public speaking and storytelling skills.

holidays.name: Physical Therapist Day
holidays.description: A day to thank the folks who help us get back on our feet, one stretch and resistance band at a time.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial awareness observance dedicated to appreciating physical therapists and the role they play in recovery, mobility, and injury prevention.
holidays.funFact: Physical therapy has roots in ancient Greece, where Hippocrates is said to have used massage and hydrotherapy to treat patients around 460 BC.
